To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Flt1 is cleaved by ADAM 10 and ADAM-17 and that this cleavage is regulated by PKC activation, VEGFR2 levels and the Flt-1 intracellular domain.
Flt1 is cleaved by ADAM10 and/or ADAM17, and this cleavage is regulated by VEGFR and Flt1 intracellular domains.
Flt1 N-terminally is cleaved by ADAM10 and/or ADAM17 and that the cleavage is regulated by the intracellular domain of Flt1, by VEGFR and by PKC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of Flt1 cleaving and the release of the N-terminal extracellular domain.
the regulation of the VEGFR2/Flt1 receptor complex.
understanding how Flt1 is regulated and how the Flt1 intracellular domain regulates Flt1 cleavability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Flt1 cleavages is a dynamic process regulated by VEGFR-2, the Flt1 intracellular region and the ADAM10 and 17 metalloproteolytic enzymes.
the ectodomain of Flk1 is released via the action of ADAM10/17, and that this release is regulated by VEGFR1, the VEGFR1 intracellular domain, and the proteasome.
the ectodomain of Fl1 can be released by cleavage of Fl1 by ADAM10 or ADAM17 and that this cleavage can be stimulated by PKC activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Flt1 cleaved to release its ectodomain is a VEGF-dependent mechanism for regulating the availability of the VEGFR1 receptor for binding and signalling.

the cleavage and release of Flt1 from the cell surface can be regulated by PKC and c-CBL, the abundance of Fltl can be controlled by ADAM10 and/or ADAM17 and the release of Flt and sFlt1 can be modulated by the abundance of VEGFR2.
the Flt1 intracellular domain contains a degradation domain and a VEGF receptor 2 binding domain which can regulate the cleavage and release of the ectodomain of Fltl.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cleavage of the Flt1 receptor is a regulated process and that the intracellular portion is required for the cleavage process.
the N-terminal cleavage of Fl-1 and the release of sFlt-1 can be regulated by the Flt-1 intracellular domain.
Flt1 can be cleaved by ADAM10 or ADAM17 and that the cytosol contains a degradation domain that can be regulated by c-CBL and PKC.
